gloss: to stare at; to gaze fixedly at

definitions.gloss: to stare at; to gaze fixedly at; to watch intently
definitions.explanation: To look at something or someone with a steady, unmoving gaze for an extended period, often with concentration, curiosity, or intensity.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はじっと{私|わたし}の{顔|かお}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: She stared fixedly at my face.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{水槽|すいそう}の{中|なか}の{魚|さかな}をじっと{見|み}ている。
examples.english: The child is gazing intently at the fish in the tank.

examples.japanese: あまりじっと{見|み}られると{緊張|きんちょう}してしまう。
examples.english: I get nervous when someone stares at me too intently.

notes:
Combines the adverb じっと (motionlessly, fixedly) with {見|み}る (to look). The expression emphasizes a sustained, unwavering gaze. じっと itself means "still, without moving" and appears in many other combinations.

RELATED PATTERNS WITH じっと:
- じっとする — to stay still, to not move
- じっと{我慢|がまん}する — to endure patiently without reacting
- じっと{待|ま}つ — to wait patiently without moving
- じっと{耐|た}える — to endure stoically

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見|み}つめる — to gaze at, to stare (single verb; more romantic or emotional nuance)
- {凝視|ぎょうし}する — to stare intently (formal/literary)
- じろじろ{見|み}る — to stare rudely, to ogle (negative nuance; implies impoliteness)
- ちらちら{見|み}る — to glance repeatedly (furtive, quick looks)

USAGE:
じっと{見|み}る is neutral in tone — it can describe concentration, fascination, worry, or deep thought. Whether the staring is rude or not depends on context, unlike じろじろ{見|み}る which is always negative.
